definition: Formal theory, in this historical aesthetic sense, is the view that beauty depends chiefly on form and its fitness for our mental powers rather than on ideal, emotional, or other interesting content. It treats judgments of beauty as grounded in formal relations such as strength, identity, opposition, or proportion, while setting aside qualities like the noble, pathetic, or touching as not properly part of beauty itself.
